name: Example: Identifying Parts of Cramer's Rule
problem:
Consider the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}9x+3y-6z=8 \\ -6x+4y+2z=3 \\ 5x-5y-15z=10.\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, $x=\dfrac{D_x}{D}$, where $D$ is the determinant of the coefficient matrix and $D_x=$
worked_solution:
We are given the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}9x+3y+(-6)z=8 \\ (-6)x+4y+2z=3 \\ 5x+(-5)y+(-15)z=10.\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of the coefficient matrix is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14059591/assets/00a69fe1d48b41e376971f3669ae51668733d36dfda18c0f9cc736d5d071a441.png)

Now, to construct $D_x$, we replace the first column of the coefficient matrix by the right-hand side column of the given system:
